findings.title: Surface-quenching inference does not state the required hardenable material
findings.actualZh: 随后迅速冷却，可以得到表面层硬度较高而内部仍保持韧性的淬火零件。
findings.actualEn: Rapid cooling can then harden the surface layer while the inner layers retain toughness.
findings.problem: The surrounding discussion identifies only a conducting part and the rapid heating/cooling sequence. Conductivity and surface-localized heating alone do not establish that the material undergoes quench hardening. The source/draft has not restricted the workpiece to suitable hardenable steel or another alloy/process with the required transformation.
findings.independentReasoning: Electromagnetic surface heating and thermal localization describe energy delivery. Surface hardness after cooling additionally depends on material and the thermal/metallurgical cycle. A pure copper conductor can exhibit induction heating without acquiring a steel-like quench-hardened surface; changing the heating method alone cannot supply the missing material transformation.
findings.minimalRequiredAction: Qualify the hardening sentence in both locales by suitable hardenable material and appropriate heating/cooling conditions, for example hardenable steel. Preserve the source's surface-hardening use, relatively cool/tough core description and machinery application rather than deleting them.
findings.suggestedZh: 对于适合淬火硬化的钢材，在适当的表面加热和冷却条件下，随后迅速冷却可以提高表层硬度，同时使内部保持所需韧性。
findings.suggestedEn: For steel suitable for quench hardening, appropriate surface-heating and cooling conditions can increase surface hardness while retaining the required core toughness.
findings.affectedOnlyFollowup: Only changed /prose/19/text and any genuinely changed adjacent anchors require follow-up; no source-page, figure or whole-text replay.

findings.title: Dielectric heating retains molecular vibration without identifying energy dissipation
findings.actualZh: 电容器的高频电场也可以用于加热电介质，原书以电介质分子的振动说明这种加热过程。
findings.actualEn: A high-frequency electric field in a capacitor can also heat a dielectric; the source explains this through molecular vibration in the material.
findings.problem: Source attribution is preserved, but its molecular-motion statement remains the only causal explanation of heating. Oscillating polarization/molecular response by itself does not establish dissipative heating. The modern explanation needs suitable material losses; the corrected depth/uniformity caveat addresses a different issue.
findings.independentReasoning: An ideal lossless dielectric can store and return field energy during each cycle without net heating. Heating requires absorption/dissipation, such as dielectric loss associated with lagging polarization and other applicable material losses. It is therefore insufficient to explain heat solely by vibration while leaving dissipation unstated.
findings.minimalRequiredAction: Retain the source's explanation as attributed historical wording, then add a brief accurate modern clarification that losses in suitable materials convert field energy to heat. Keep the interior-heating application and the existing nonuniform-depth caveat.
findings.suggestedZhClarification: 用现代术语说，这种加热需要材料中的损耗机制，例如极化响应滞后造成的介电损耗；理想无损电介质不会仅因电场交变而持续发热。
findings.suggestedEnClarification: In modern terms, heating requires losses in the material, such as dielectric loss from a lagging polarization response; an ideal lossless dielectric does not continuously heat merely because the field alternates.
findings.affectedOnlyFollowup: Only changed /prose/20/text and genuinely affected anchors require follow-up. Do not reopen figure61/62 or replay passed text.
